subject: Lumenware integration ops & schema qualification
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex@lumenware.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-23T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Lumenware integration ops & schema qualification

Hi Alex — great call earlier, thanks for walking through the workload. This note is a short technical recap plus a few concrete questions so our engineers can prepare for the deep-dive. I attached a simple sample_schema.json (see attachment) that sketches the request/response fields we typically use — please take a quick look and flag gaps.

Recap (what we heard):
- Primary use case: interactive support assistant inside Lumenware console (low-latency streaming for agent assists) + nightly batch summarization of session logs (higher-throughput completions).
- Data plane: customer events + search index for context (embeddings + reranker).
- Security: must support customer-managed keys (KMS) for Private deployment, plus SOC2 evidence.

Open questions / asks for deep-dive:
1) SDK & auth: do you prefer API keys per service account, or OAuth-style short-lived tokens for end-user impersonation? If the latter, we should review token exchange flows.
2) Routing / deployment: do you want hosted inference for quick POC or start with Dedicated capacity? Any restrictions on region (we heard US-only)?
3) Structured output / tool-calling: will you want to call internal tools (search, ticket create) from the model output (tool-calling)? If yes, we recommend the structured JSON return pattern we sketched in sample_schema.json.
4) Embeddings & reranker: expected queries/sec for semantic search and average context size (documents per query). This drives batching/throughput recommendations.
5) Request/response schema specifics:
   - Chat vs completions: interactive assistant should use chat streaming (server-sent events) to reduce latency and support partial results; nightly jobs can use completions with larger max_tokens.
   - Tokenization & max_tokens: we usually recommend setting max_tokens conservatively for streaming (e.g., 256-512) and offloading long summaries to batch flows. Do you have strict token limits?
   - Stop sequences: any business-critical stop markers (e.g., "---END---") you must enforce?
   - Streaming semantics: do you need incremental tool calls (invoke tool while streaming) or post-response tool invocation?

Proposed next steps:
- Tech deep-dive (60m) with your infra and our serving/runtime engineer — suggested times in the calendar invite I'm sending.
- We’ll share a short runbook (auth snippets + recommended SDK usage) and a draft mutual action plan ahead of the call.

Attachments: sample_schema.json (simple JSON schema), redwood-sdk-auth-snippets.txt

Thanks — happy to adjust based on your priorities.

— Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
naomi@redwood.com
(Attachment: sample_schema.json)
From: Alex Rivera <alex@lumenware.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Cc: Lumenware Sales Ops <salesops@lumenware.com>
Date: 2026-07-23T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Lumenware integration ops & schema qualification

Thanks Naomi — this is helpful. Quick answers inline: 

1) Auth: for POC we can use per-service API keys, but long-term we will need user-level short-lived tokens (we plan to surface the assistant inside our app per end-user). We'll want a token-exchange pattern so our backend mints short-lived tokens for the client.

2) Routing: POC — hosted is fine. Production — we'd prefer Dedicated/GPU-reserved in us-east-1 (low latency to our infra).

3) Tool-calling: yes, we want the assistant to be able to call internal search and ticket creation. Ideally the model returns a structured payload that includes an action field + arguments. The sample_schema looks close.

4) Embeddings: expected steady-state qps ~ 10-20 with spikes to 80 during peak. Average document size for context is ~600 tokens; we plan to keep the top 20 candidates for reranking.

5) Schema specifics:
   - Chat vs completions: agree — chat streaming for interactive; completions for batch summarization.
   - Tokenization & max_tokens: 512 for live responses is a good starting point; for nightly summaries we'll allow up to 4096. Question: do you support automatic prefix (KV) caching across sessions to cut token costs?
   - Stop sequences: we'll use an explicit marker "<END_RESPONSE>" when the tool should stop.
   - Streaming semantics: incremental tool calls would be ideal (e.g., model signals a partial result, we can call search before finalizing). Is that supported or do you recommend a canonical pattern?

I attached our very rough arch doc (lumenware-arch-v1.pdf). Happy to join the deep-dive.

— Alex
Alex Rivera
Head of Product, Lumenware
alex@lumenware.com
(Attachment: lumenware-arch-v1.pdf)
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-23T13:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Lumenware integration ops & schema qualification

Naomi / Monica — quick internal notes before the deep-dive: 

- Auth pattern: we'll prepare two snippets — 1) short-lived token exchange (recommended for user-level sessions) and 2) service-level API key example for POCs. Put both in redwood-sdk-auth-snippets.txt.
- Routing: show them Hosted vs Dedicated latency and cost delta for typical qps (we have a one-pager). If they want us-east-1 Dedicated that's available as a capacity plan — Monica, pls pull Dedicated pricing/commit tiers.
- Streaming/tool-calls: our runtime supports streaming + tool-calling semantics. Best practice is: have the model emit a structured action block (JSON) as it streams; the orchestration layer buffers until a complete action payload is seen (we can point to the streaming examples). For incremental tool calls, we recommend a small middleware that can invoke search on partial results — we'll demo this.
- Embeddings/Batching: for 10-80 qps recommend batched embedding requests (batch size 32-64) with a dedicated embedding pool; discuss vector DB tradeoffs during the call.

I'll prepare a short demo that shows: streaming chat, structured tool output, and a reranker invocation (embed + nn-descent). Naomi, I'll add Marissa (engineering) to the invite for the deep-dive.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Staff Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks Alex — great context and the architecture doc is useful. Confirming next steps / action items before the deep-dive (putting timelines):

1) We (Redwood) will send:
   - redwood-sdk-auth-snippets.txt (API key + token-exchange examples) — EOD tomorrow.
   - small runbook that maps chat-streaming vs completions and recommended max_tokens/stop patterns for each flow.
   - demo: streaming chat -> structured action JSON -> incremental search invocation (Ben/Marissa to run).

2) Lumenware will send: lumenware-arch-v1.pdf (received), and any compliance checklist if Dedicated/Private is required. Please also confirm peak qps windows and any regional restrictions.

3) Deep-dive: booked for 2026-07-27 10:00-11:00 PT (invite sent). Please add any engineers you want on the call.

Quick clarifications before the call:
- We'll support prefix/KV cache to reduce token consumption; we'll show a small config that pins short-term session context to the KV cache.
- For incremental tool-calling, our recommended pattern is: model emits {"action": "search", "args": {"query": "..."}} within the stream; orchestration detects complete JSON block and fires the search. We can show how to surface partial results to the user while the reranker runs.

Attachments included here: sample_schema.json (our suggested structured output), redwood-sdk-auth-snippets.txt (will be populated).

If that looks right, I'll leave the deep-dive invite as-is. Looking forward to it.

— Naomi
